Name: Durumi Hut - Harvest Helpers and Bucket Watering
Author: asb3967
Description:
[b]Durumi Hut 1.4.0 — Teach the helpers[/b]
Build a home for red-bereted Durumi helpers at Robin's shop. The same crew harvests crops, carries water from its well and shares meals and a bed inside the hut. This update lets your farmer teach them through the existing Skills tab.

[b]Teach farming from your Skills tab[/b]
After completing a Durumi Hut, open the player's Skills tab. A Durumi face beneath the Farming row marks the helpers' learned level. Hover over it to see the current level and teaching limit; click it to teach all currently completed Durumi Huts. The faint face marks how far the helpers can learn. If huts have learned different levels, the face shows the lowest one. Teach again after gaining Farming levels or building another hut.

The limit is your [b]base Farming level minus two, from level 0 to level 8[/b]. A farmer at level 10 can teach level 8. Lessons first become useful at Farming level 3. Food and other temporary skill buffs do not raise the limit. Each hut saves its learned level and teacher.

[b]Update note: helpers use Farming level 0 until taught.[/b] This applies to existing huts when updating from 1.3 or an earlier version. Visit the Farming row after updating your farm.

The learned level affects the game's crop-quality rolls and any harvest quantity that depends on Farming level. Fertilizer retains its normal effect. Storage, overflow and the usual harvest restrictions continue to follow the game's Junimo rules. Helper harvests do not give the farmer Farming XP.

The crew still performs crop harvesting and physical bucket watering. Teaching does not add another automated job. Profession sale bonuses follow the selling farmer's normal rules. The proposed 40%-to-20% profession transfer has no matching effect in these jobs; Artisan processing and sale bonuses are not taught in this update.

[b]Life inside the hut — retained from 1.3[/b]
Walk through the hut door to meet the same helpers who work in your fields. At midday they can share a meal, and at 9 pm or later each helper settles at their own pillow beneath the patchwork quilt. The base hut uses two places in the shared bed; an expanded hut uses three.

The room follows the creator's illustrated layout: a continuous kitchen counter, central dining table, shared canopy bed, bookcases, tea table by the hearth and a study. Chairs and bedding have separate foreground pieces so helpers sit behind the slats and sleep beneath the quilt. Paths lead to their actual furniture and seats. Meals and washing are visual routines; they do not consume crops or produce cooking items.

The indoor harvest box opens the hut's shared 36-slot storage. The study control pauses or resumes harvesting. Inspect the globe, bookcase or kitchen stove for different lines. Reading, writing and page-turning share book poses; winter indoor activities use directional poses for books, meals, drinks and washing.

[b]Rain and winter[/b]
Rainy mornings start indoors. If rain begins while the helpers are outside, they wear yellow raincoats and physically return through their door. Idle winter helpers rest inside, leaving in warm clothes only when there is actual watering work and returning afterward. Indoor and outdoor helpers are one native population, with no extra work crew.

Harvesters rest in rain, winter and on traditional festival days. The well upgrade's watering runs independently from 6 am until 7 pm on dry days, including winter and festivals when eligible crops need water. Rain stops watering.

[b]Build and upgrade[/b]
Robin offers the hut without wizard-quest, year or season unlocks. Normal shop hours and construction scheduling apply. The original Junimo Hut remains available.

[list]
[*]Base: a 13×13 area centered on the door, up to 2 helpers. Costs 20,000g, 200 stone, 9 starfruit and 100 fiber; takes 2 days.
[*]First upgrade: a 17×17 area and up to 3 helpers. Costs 5,000g, 100 wood and 100 stone; takes 1 day.
[*]Second upgrade: the same area and crew, plus a small well and bucket watering. Costs 10,000g, 200 stone, 5 iron bars and 10 hardwood; takes 2 days.
[/list]Each exterior building occupies 3×2 tiles. The working area includes the building.

[b]Physical bucket watering[/b]
Helpers fill buckets at the well, carry water to a crop and pour before its soil becomes wet. One bucket waters up to 8 targets before refilling. Filling, walking and pouring take time, and the same maximum of 3 helpers also handles harvesting.

Growing crops, trellis crops, wild seeds and outdoor garden pots are eligible. Dead crops, empty soil, already-wet soil and crops that need no water are skipped. A reachable route is required. The harvest toggle is independent of watering.

[b]Install and update[/b]
Use your own Stardew Valley 1.6.15 installation and SMAPI 4.5.2. Content Patcher is not required. Close the game, move the old DurumiHut folder outside Mods, then extract the new DurumiHut folder into Mods. Existing standalone installations can replace DurumiHut-Standalone/Mods/DurumiHut. Launch through SMAPI. Existing huts remain in the save; teach them from the Farming row after updating.

This is the standard mod ZIP with source and build instructions. No proprietary Stardew game files are distributed. Install SMAPI from [url=https://smapi.io/]its official site[/url].

[b]Previous installer warning:[/b] Nexus quarantined the earlier optional Windows installer. Its executable has detections from multiple security engines, and those detections have not been established as false positives. The replacement installer remains withheld. Use the standard ZIP; do not disable protection or bypass quarantine to run the old executable.

Personal items obstructed by the updated room's walls, fixtures or exit are recovered with their contents at the Lost and Found in the Mayor's Manor. A farmer loaded at an obsolete blocked position moves to the entrance. To remove the mod, empty storage, leave the room, demolish all Durumi Huts through Robin while the mod is enabled, and save a day. Close the game, then remove the mod folder.

[b]Twelve languages[/b]
Construction menus, furniture, room interactions and teaching follow the language selected in Stardew Valley: English, German, Spanish, French, Hungarian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Turkish and Simplified Chinese. A quick-start guide in all twelve languages is included. Translations are AI-assisted; full native-speaker proofreading is not claimed.

[b]AI disclosure and credits[/b]
This is an [b]unofficial Drami fan creation[/b]. Durumi is a user-defined ten-year-old child with an androgynous appearance, a red beret and short white hair. The player farmer and ordinary Junimos retain their original appearances.

The commissioning user supplied the character setting, Life Pack and illustrated room layout. OpenAI Codex and GPT-6 Astra assisted code, review, translations, documentation and testing. OpenAI's built-in image generation created or edited original helper and hut artwork. AI-Generated Content and AI Media apply. Gameplay screenshots are actual game captures; labeled concept artwork is illustrative. No endorsement by the game developer or streamer is claimed.

Stardew Valley belongs to ConcernedApe. SMAPI is maintained by Pathoschild and contributors. The mod loads the game's assets from the player's installation. The archive includes the mod's source and build instructions.

[b]Validation and limits[/b]
The supported inspection environment is Windows single-player, Stardew Valley 1.6.15 and SMAPI 4.5.2. Multiplayer, compatibility with other Junimo overhauls and every mod combination are unverified. Please report reproducible issues with relevant SMAPI logs, keeping private save and account data out of public posts.
